findings.text: low: the agent read builds its rows with no repo_dir — index_discovery calls metadata_index.index_rows(docs_dir, project, revalidate=True) (mcp_views.py:1154) — so the build stamps each row with metadata_index._stat_stamps while the served process stamps with stamps_for (git-aware), and both share ONE persisted file keyed only by project and docs_dir (metadata_index.py:396, no with_git term). On a rewritten document the agent build re-parses it with stat stamps and, because build.changed is then true, rewrites the shared persisted entry (metadata_index.py:192), so the served payload's created/edited for that document move: reproduced at 89b2398ba in a git-archive scratch copy (reviewer-stamp-divergence.log) with a tracked file whose git first-commit stamp is 1500000000 — a served build reads created=1500000000, an agent read after a rewrite writes persisted created=1790815424, and a later cold served build reuses it and reads created=1790815424. This violates the invariant stamps_for's own docstring states (the two payloads 'cannot disagree on one document's timestamps). The repair is to pass repo_dir and the git maps into the agent read's index_rows call, as the served path does.

low: the reviewed record's head gate log carries rev=2cc4f81a662bcfaa881578ab66063b9fb1f4e0a0 on its header line while the tree it measured is the working tree committed as 3881bbd7c (its own parenthetical says so), so a reader who takes the log's revision field at face value attributes the 114-passed result to a superseded commit. The after_suite revision field in the manifest is prose ('working tree over 2cc4f81a, committed as 3881bbd7c') rather than the sha the log should name. Recording the committed sha on the header would remove the ambiguity.

justifications.durability: The cold-path zero is properly held: a positive control proves the counters fire, the declared negative control proves they catch a return to discover_plans, and the two rewritten-document tests fail when revalidate is removed and pass when it is present, so a later regression is caught. The fixtures are deterministic (temporary trees and config home, fixed slugs, mtime bumped explicitly so a re-stat sees the move, no date-derived literal). The deduction: the stamp-source divergence this change introduces is unguarded — no case compares the agent read's persisted stamps against the served rule, so the module's own stated invariant (stamps_for's docstring: the two payloads 'cannot disagree on one document's timestamps') fails without an assertion.
justifications.evidence: The measure is genuine and doubly guarded, and I reproduced it independently. test_the_cold_build_parses_every_document_once is a positive control (the cold build parses all 200 documents, so the counters are shown to fire before the zero is trusted); the declared negative control routes index_discovery back through discover_plans and fails; I re-ran the head gate myself at 89b2398ba for 114 passed EXIT=0 (reviewer-head-gate.log) and reproduced the negative control on a git-archive scratch copy of that head for (2, 200, 0) == (0, 0, 0), 4 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1 (reviewer-negative-control.log). I also falsified the revalidation fix by dropping revalidate=True in a scratch copy: both rewritten-document tests fail (MUT_EXIT=1) and pass with it (HEAD_EXIT=0). The deduction: the reviewed head-gate.log's header names rev=2cc4f81a6 while the tree it measured was the working tree committed as 3881bbd7c, so the log's own revision field names a superseded commit and only the parenthetical carries the truth.
justifications.fit: index_discovery has one responsibility and is named by mechanism; revalidate rides the existing index_rows as a default-off keyword so the served path that the change watch already covers is unchanged, and the helpers are _index_project_summary, _index_sprint_state and _aggregate_version. The four commits carry conventional subjects and substantive bodies, no plan, sprint or ticket label, and no AI trailer (git log -1 --format=%B cleaned of 'co-authored-by'); the code carries no version or phase name.
